title: the prayer you know by heart
hookLine: a king who tried to take by force, and the prayer he's remembered for: asking only for a clear mind
carry: a prayer for a clear mind

cards: Om bhur bhuvah svah. If you grew up in a Hindu home, there's a good chance you can say the rest without thinking. Maybe someone said it every morning.
Maybe it played at every puja. Now the hard part: what does it ask for? Most people go quiet.
The answer starts with a king who wanted something he couldn't take. First, a guess.

teach.b: Long ago a powerful king, Vishvamitra, stopped with his army at the forest home of the sage Vasishtha. The sage fed every soldier, thanks to a wondrous cow that could give anything. The king wanted her.
He offered herds of cattle, gold, jewels. The sage said no. So the king tried to take her by force, and lost: his armies and his weapons failed against one sage with a staff.
Stung, he gave up his throne and spent years in practice, failing and starting over, until at last even Vasishtha honored him as a great sage.
Tradition names Vishvamitra as the seer of the prayer many Hindus say at dawn: the Gayatri. Listen to what it asks. Bhur bhuvah svah: earth, sky, and beyond.
Tat savitur varenyam: that worthy light of Savitar, the sun that stirs the world awake. Bhargo devasya dhimahi: we meditate on that divine radiance.

teach.h: MAY IT WAKE UP OUR MINDS.
teach.b: Dhiyo yo nah prachodayat: may it wake up and guide our minds. Not a cow. Not a kingdom.
Not to win. A clear mind. The man who tried to take everything by force is remembered for a prayer that asks only to see.

teach.h: MANTRA — A TOOL FOR THE MIND.
teach.b: That's a mantra: man, to think, and tra, a tool. Some traditions teach the Gayatri at a coming-of-age ceremony; in many homes, everyone simply says it.
If you grew up saying it without the meaning, you weren't doing it wrong. The night before an exam or a hard talk, it doesn't ask for the result. It asks for a mind that sees straight.

how: Many Hindus say the Gayatri mantra at dawn, and often at dusk, sometimes a set number of times on a mala; it opens with om bhur bhuvah svah.

games.q: a friend says a mantra is a magic spell: say the words and you get what you want. what's closer to what the word means?
o: a tool for the mind, said on purpose.
games.why: man, to think, and tra, a tool. the Gayatri doesn't ask for things at all; it asks for a mind woken up.

practice: Three breaths with the bell. Breathe in. As you breathe out, say the Gayatri once, slowly, out loud or in your head, or just its last line: dhiyo yo nah prachodayat, may it wake up and guide our minds.
